title: Maya Character Rigging - Part 9. create FK, IK and Skin leg joint

steps.goal: Create the initial leg skin joint chain from hip to toe tip
common_mistakes: A perfectly straight limb chain makes later IK unpredictable (the knee can flip). (community: Autodesk Community: Arm bending wrong way | community: Polycount: IK joints need a slight bend / straight chain problem)
steps.result: A five-joint leg skeleton chain is created consisting of hip, knee, ankle, ball, and toe joints.

how_to.text: Open Skeleton > Create Joints menu item.
how_to.evidence: Instructor opens Skeleton > Create Joints.

how_to.text: In the Side view, click sequentially at the hip position, knee position, ankle position, ball position, and toe tip position.
how_to.evidence: Instructor places joint centers in Side view.

how_to.text: Press Enter to finalize the joint chain creation.
how_to.evidence: Chain is completed upon pressing Enter.

check.text: Check that a 5-joint chain is visible inside the character leg mesh.
check.evidence: Joint hierarchy is visible inside character leg in viewports.

steps.goal: Orient the skin leg joint chain axes
common_mistakes: Letting Maya orient automatically on a curved chain can flip axes, because it does not know which way is 'up' for the joints; choose a Secondary Axis World Orientation to fix the up direction. (community: University of Washington CSE 460: Orienting joints | community: Maya: Orient Joint Options)
Orienting the joints after skinning moves the rest pose of the skeleton; orient before binding. (author: no source)
assumptions: Before this: The joint chain exists and is parented root to tip.
Before this: Select the root joint of the chain first, and turn on 'Orient children of selected joints' if the whole chain should change.
steps.result: The local axes of the skin joint chain are oriented consistently down the joint chain.

steps.goal: Add custom FK_IK_Switch attribute to the switch control object
common_mistakes: Switching modes mid-animation makes the limb jump back to where the other chain's pose was, unless the FK controls are first matched to the IK pose (or the reverse). (community: tech-artists.org: Automatic FK/IK switching in a Maya rig)
steps.result: A custom float attribute named FK_IK_Switch (range 0 to 1) is added to l_switch_GEO.

how_to.text: Select 'l_switch_GEO'.
how_to.evidence: Selects l_switch_GEO.

how_to.text: Open Channel Box menu Edit > Add Attribute.
how_to.evidence: Opens Add Attribute window from Channel Box menu.

how_to.text: Set Long Name to 'FK_IK_Switch'.
how_to.evidence: Types FK_IK_Switch into Attribute Name.

how_to.text: Ensure Data Type is Float, set Minimum to 0, Maximum to 1, Default to 0, and click Add.
how_to.evidence: Sets Min 0, Max 1, Default 0 and clicks Add.

check.text: Check Channel Box of l_switch_GEO to see 'FK_IK_Switch' attribute added at the bottom.
check.evidence: FK_IK_Switch attribute is visible in Channel Box.

steps.visual_evidence: Add Attribute window is used to add FK_IK_Switch float attribute with min 0 and max 1.

steps.goal: Test FK and IK switching behavior on the skin leg joints
steps.result: Toggling FK_IK_Switch seamlessly switches the skin leg chain driver between FK (value 0) and IK (value 1).

how_to.text: Select 'l_switch_GEO' and set FK_IK_Switch attribute to 0 in Channel Box.
how_to.evidence: Sets FK_IK_Switch to 0.

how_to.text: Rotate FK hip joint to confirm skin leg follows FK joints.
how_to.evidence: Rotates FK hip joint; skin joints follow.

how_to.text: Set FK_IK_Switch attribute to 1 in Channel Box and rotate IK joint to confirm skin leg follows IK joints.
how_to.evidence: Sets FK_IK_Switch to 1; skin joints follow IK chain movement.

check.text: Verify skin joints follow FK when switch is 0 and follow IK when switch is 1.
check.evidence: Instructor demonstrates skin joints following FK and IK successively.
